HEADER:
Date: 2025-04-02
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording id: ff-20250402-tycho-01
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Samuel (Redwood SE), Rachel (Tycho Head of Security), Marco (Tycho Platform), Aisha (Tycho Privacy Counsel)

SUMMARY:
Quick security & data-handling review focused on prompt retention, PII/PHI handling, encryption/KMS options, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log format and retention, plus confirm "no training on customer data" commitments. Next: send SOC2, data-flow diagram, and sample logs.

TOPICS NOTED (auto):
- SOC 2 / ISO attestation status
- Encryption at rest / CMK options
- Prompt & content retention and deletion APIs
- PII/PHI redaction and controls
- SSO (SAML/SCIM) and RBAC mapping
- Audit logs: retention, export, schema
- Data residency (EU/US) and private deployment options

ACTION ITEMS (recorded):
- Maya to share SOC2 report and compliance pack (see next steps)
- Samuel to send architecture/dataflow and audit-log sample
- Marco to provide PII list and retention SLA

TRANSCRIPT BODY:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. Quick roll call — I am Maya, AE, and Sam is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Rachel (Tycho): Hi, Rachel here, head of security at Tycho. Marco and Aisha are on. Thanks.
[00:12] Samuel (Redwood): thanks rachel, hi everyone. We wanted to go through the specifics on retention, encryption and the "no train" question up front.
[00:20] Marco (Tycho): Yes, main ask: we are heavily regulated, we process sensitive financial data and occasionally PHI-similar payloads for member support — we need strong assurances about prompt retention and that redwood won't use our data to tune models.
[00:30] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely, high level: Redwood provides a committed no-training-on-customer-data policy for enterprise contracts and we have options for no-persistent-retention on hosted as well as private deployments. We'll share the contract language but to paraphrase: we don't include customer prompts/outputs in training corpora unless explicit opt-in for fine-tuning.
[00:45] Aisha (Tycho): Can you point me to the legal language? verbal is fine but Aisha wants actual clause we can reference in review.
[00:50] Maya (Redwood): Yep, I'll send the SOC2 pack and the standard DPA addendum with the training clause — Samuel will follow with architecture diagrams that show how data flows and where ephemeral caching happens.
[01:05] Samuel (Redwood): On the runtime side, there are three layers where customers control data: request transit (TLS), in-memory KV-cache for generation which we can disable/flush per-request, and persistent logs/telemetry which are stored with encryption at rest. We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS and HSM options for Private deployments.
[01:25] Rachel (Tycho): The CMK option is critical. We need to be able to revoke keys quickly in case of incident and ensure logs are unreadable without our key material. How does that work for hosted vs dedicated?
[01:35] Samuel (Redwood): For Hosted, we support envelope encryption with customer KMS in supported clouds — you provide a CMK, we wrap tokens and persistent artifacts. For Dedicated and Private, you can bring keys and we can configure HSM-backed storage for logs and model caches. There's a small caveat around ephemeral in-memory caches — those are encrypted in memory and can be wiped on request.
[01:55] Marco (Tycho): when you say cache wipe, is there an API to force flush KV cache and purge request traces? We need that for legal holds and data minimization controls.
[02:05] Samuel (Redwood): Yes, API exists — POST /v1/admin/purge-session or similar — we'll share exact endpoint. It accepts session id or customer id and returns purge token. Note: cross-tenant logs are not purged, only the customer's persistent artifacts.
[02:22] Aisha (Tycho): About audit logs: we have long retention regulatory obligations — 7 years for some records — how configurable are audit exports and retention? Also chain-of-custody for deleted records?
[02:34] Maya (Redwood): Audit logs can be exported to your storage (S3, GCS) daily or streamed. Retention is configurable per-tenant on Dedicated and Private; on Hosted we have default retention (90 days) with longer-retention paid add-ons. For deletions we provide deletion events and an immutable deletion log with signature for chain-of-custody.
[02:55] Rachel (Tycho): 90 days is short for us; we'll need 7 years on some tables. Is there an add-on for that on hosted?
[03:03] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we offer an extended retention package that pushes audit exports to customer bucket and keeps minimal indexed metadata for search. That can meet the 7 year requirement if you store the exported logs in your own account, which you can.
[03:20] Marco (Tycho): Okay. About SSO/SCIM — we use Okta and need to map roles to internal RBAC: developer vs ops vs read-only compliance. How granular is the role model?
[03:30] Samuel (Redwood): Our SSO supports SAML and OIDC; provisioning via SCIM is supported for Dedicated/Private and for enterprise hosted customers. RBAC is hierarchical: org-admin, billing-admin, model-deployer, viewer, plus custom roles. You can restrict routes (e.g., inference-only tokens) and control export privileges.
[03:50] Aisha (Tycho): Do you provide audit trails for admin actions (who rotated keys, who created a private endpoint)? Those must be immutable and tamper-evident.
[03:58] Samuel (Redwood): Yes, admin actions are logged with actor identity. For Dedicated/Private we can forward logs to your SIEM; we also have signed log digests for tamper evidence on request.
[04:14] Rachel (Tycho): Encryption specifics: in transit TLS 1.2+? in rest AES-256? and KMS providers?
[04:22] Maya (Redwood): TLS 1.2 minimum — TLS 1.3 preferred. At rest we use AES-256-GCM by default. KMS integrations include AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault; on-prem HSM via PKCS#11 for private deployments.
[04:35] Marco (Tycho): About data residency: we need EU-only processing for EU customers. Can you guarantee that for hosted?
[04:42] Samuel (Redwood): Yes we have region pinning. Hosted tenants can be pinned to EU region and all inference and logs remain in-region. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private where control is absolute.
[04:55] Rachel (Tycho): What about prompt retention policy — default is you keep prompts for X days? And can we opt-out so no prompt content is ever stored?
[05:05] Maya (Redwood): Default: ephemeral caching for 24 hours for performance; persistent logs are 90 days on hosted. We offer a zero-retention option for enterprise: no persistent storage of prompts/outputs, only encrypted ephemeral memory for the duration of the request. For debugging we allow structured traces that can be redacted; these are optional.
[05:22] Marco (Tycho): Are prompts ever used to improve models? We need explicit confirmation they are not used for training.
[05:28] Maya (Redwood): Confirmed: Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs for model training by default. For any fine-tuning or research use, there is an explicit opt-in flow and contractual terms. We'll provide DPA and training clause language.
[05:42] Aisha (Tycho): Good, please put that in writing. Also need to know about pseudonymization and redaction support — can Redwood automatically redact likely PII?
[05:52] Samuel (Redwood): We have a redact pipeline plugin that does deterministic redaction and token masking; customers can supply rules or use our prebuilt PII detectors. It's configurable and you can run redaction client-side also.
[06:06] Marco (Tycho): Client-side redaction is preferable for some flows. Is there an SDK or recommended pattern?
[06:11] Samuel (Redwood): Yes, client SDKs include a pre-request pipeline that runs PII detectors locally and masks before sending. We'll send links to the SDK docs and sample code.
[06:22] Rachel (Tycho): Logging and telemetry: we need to ensure that sensitive fields are never logged. How do logs handle request payloads?
[06:29] Maya (Redwood): By default logs include metadata and hashed identifiers, not raw payloads; raw prompt text is only persisted if you enable full trace. We recommend hashed IDs and redaction for any regulated workload.
[06:44] Marco (Tycho): For e-discovery or legal hold we might need to retain content — how is legal hold handled if we requested purge earlier?
[06:52] Aisha (Tycho): yes, legal holds can conflict with deletion. We need a mechanism to suspend deletions.
[06:58] Samuel (Redwood): We support hold flags at tenant level: once a legal hold is set, purge APIs will fail and an audit event is generated. Only authorized roles can set/unset holds and it's logged with a signed event.
[07:12] Rachel (Tycho): Pen tests and external audits — do you run yearly pen tests? third-party scans?
[07:18] Maya (Redwood): We engage external pen-testers annually and run quarterly vuln scans. We also have a bug-bounty program. SOC2 Type II covers the infosec controls; ISO 27001 is in progress — we'll send the timeline.
[07:33] Marco (Tycho): Can we get a red team report or at least the high-level findings from recent tests?
[07:38] Maya (Redwood): We can share redacted summaries and remediation timelines. Full reports are available under an NDA.
[07:46] Aisha (Tycho): Incident response — what are your breach notification timelines?
[07:50] Samuel (Redwood): We have a 72-hour notification SLA for confirmed infra breaches affecting customer data; for suspected incidents we notify customers in preliminary form and follow up. We provide an incident contact and runbooks to customers with Dedicated/Private plans.
[08:05] Rachel (Tycho): Ok. A few nitty-gritty items: format for audit logs, can you push to our SIEM, and schema for events?
[08:13] Samuel (Redwood): We send JSON events with timestamp (RFC3339), actor_id, action, resource, region, request_id, and optional metadata. We'll attach the exact schema and examples — sample event: {"ts":"2025-04-01T12:00:00Z","actor":"rachel@example.com","action":"key.rotate","resource":"/keys/abc123","request_id":"req-..."}.
[08:36] Marco (Tycho): Will logs include prompt content?
[08:39] Samuel (Redwood): No by default. Prompt content is only in full-trace logs if you opt-in. In exports we can redact content fields or omit them entirely.
[08:49] Maya (Redwood): Also note we have a structured search index for traced sessions — index contains metadata fields for search but not raw prompt text unless enabled.
[09:00] Aisha (Tycho): For compliance evidence, can you provide signed attestations for deletion events? We mentioned chain-of-custody earlier.
[09:08] Samuel (Redwood): Yes, deletion events are signed server-side and we can provide an immutable audit of deletion requests with timestamp and actor. We'll show example signed digest in the compliance pack.
[09:22] Rachel (Tycho): Regarding model versions — can we pin a specific model binary to avoid behavior drift? And can we run a canary without exposure to prod customers?
[09:31] Maya (Redwood): Yes, pinning model version is supported. We also provide canary routes and A/B rollouts. On Dedicated/Private you can push a model image and control rollouts.
[09:44] Marco (Tycho): One more: data residency in EU plus encryption keys stored in EU — do you support keys hosted in EU KMS?
[09:52] Samuel (Redwood): Yes, we can integrate with EU region KMS endpoints and ensure keys never leave the region for hosted EU-tenants.
[10:00] Rachel (Tycho): Good. Now on retention: could you repeat the default hosted retention numbers and options for zero retention?
[10:07] Maya (Redwood): Sure — hosted default: ephemeral in-memory for real-time, persistent logs 90 days; extended export option to your bucket for longer retention; enterprise zero-retention option removes persistent storage of prompts/outputs and prevents inclusion in telemetry.
[10:20] Marco (Tycho): Are there cost implications for zero retention or CMK use?
[10:25] Maya (Redwood): Yes, zero retention increases operational cost slightly and CMK/HSM has a premium for key management and KMS calls. We'll outline pricing in the package doc.
[10:36] Aisha (Tycho): We need DPA language and the clause about not training on customer data. Please include specific wording and the process for opting in to fine tuning.
[10:44] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll send DPA and training clause; opt-in for fine-tuning requires a signed addendum and an explicit dataset approval flow.
[10:55] Rachel (Tycho): Are there any anomaly detection or data loss prevention features baked into Redwood?
[11:01] Samuel (Redwood): We have anomaly detection on usage spikes, anomalous API patterns and can integrate with your DLP to block certain payloads client-side.
[11:12] Marco (Tycho): If we run a pilot, can we do it in EU region with zero-retention and CMK?
[11:18] Maya (Redwood): Yes, that's a typical pilot for regulated customers — we'll scope it as a Dedicated pilot with those controls.
[11:26] Rachel (Tycho): Ok, timeline: we expect compliance review by mid-April, legal sign-off end of April. We might request the contract language before our compliance meeting.
[11:36] Maya (Redwood): We'll aim to send SOC2, DPA, and the architecture diagram by Friday (2025-04-04).
[11:44] Samuel (Redwood): I'll include sample audit logs, schema, and the purge API doc by Monday (2025-04-06).
[11:52] Aisha (Tycho): Thanks. We'll circulate our PII listings and retention policy draft by 2025-04-10.
[12:00] Maya (Redwood): Great. Any last questions?
[12:05] Rachel (Tycho): Nothing else from me. Thanks for the clarity.
[12:10] Marco (Tycho): All good.
[12:12] Aisha (Tycho): Thanks everyone.
[12:15] Maya (Redwood): Thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts.
